cadence_note: Requested as a last-30-days read. October 1 is when the monthly budget stepped up, so this window is the first full 30 days at the higher spend; the comparison window is mostly pre-increase (Sep 5 – Sep 30) plus Oct 1–4.
spend_scope_note: Spend in the 30-day window covers Google Ads and Meta only, the two platforms connected to the reporting dashboard. Microsoft (Bing) and LinkedIn are not in Looker; the October spend sheet shows they added $2,751.09 in calendar October (Microsoft $2,295.16, LinkedIn $455.93), for an all-channel October total of $36,573.96. See 'October, all channels' in Budget & ROI.

summary.total_leads_note: Platform-reported: 39 Google Ads conversions + 90 Meta leads. Spark (the CRM, the source of truth for real people) recorded 125 genuinely new non-agent contacts in the same 30 days (138 before removing the Oct 15 back-fill), 100 of them from paid Google, Meta or LinkedIn.
summary.google_ctr_note: Search-only click-through rate: 2,382 clicks on 31,005 search impressions. Blended with Display and YouTube it is 0.34%.
summary.answer_rate_note: 9 of 16 calls answered = 56.3% (CallRail tiles and daily table agree).
summary.narrative: The first full month at the higher budget bought more people, not cheaper ones. Google and Meta spend rose 33% to $32.4K and the CRM recorded 125 genuinely new contacts against 80 the month before (+56%), with paid Google up 38% (16 to 22) and Meta up 32% (41 to 54). LinkedIn, live only since October 28, added 24 more in its first week. Cost per CRM-verified lead from Google and Meta held flat at about $427, so the extra money scaled volume at the same price rather than buying efficiency. Quality is where the month falls short: 12 contacts are rated good today versus 10, and Meta produced just 1 of them from 62. Paid Google produced 3 and the sales center 3. Many of this window's newest contacts still carry Spark's default rating, so those quality numbers will move. On creative, the new 'Day at Mira Mar' video earned 7 leads from 5,192 views, the best rate of any video in the account, while the Yoga cuts never got enough delivery to judge. Two lines spent with nothing to show: YouTube ($1,609, zero clicks) and Display ($2,101, zero good leads). Phone calls fell from 49 to 16, almost all on Google, and the answer rate stayed at 56%.

midterm_market.headline: The midterm ad market made impressions more expensive

metrics.derivation: cost / impressions × 1000 from Meta Ads Overview
Looker Avg CPC tile; confounded by October campaign-mix changes

midterm_market.industry_context: Industry reports put 2026 midterm political ad spend at about $11–12 billion, with YouTube and Meta political spend rising from $34M a week in late July to $149M in the week of Oct 11 and YouTube costs up about 20%. Florida also had a governor's race on the ballot.
midterm_market.read: Most of the cost increase on Meta and YouTube lines up with the industry-wide political surge; Display, which political buyers largely skipped, got cheaper. Site users fell 5% even as spend rose 33%, consistent with pricier impressions, but lead volume still rose and Election Day (Nov 3) was the busiest real day of the window. Several of our own changes landed in October too (budget increase, new creative, landing-page switch, LinkedIn launch), so the election explains part of the cost rise, not all of it.
midterm_market.next: Political ads clear out after Nov 3. If cost per click and cost per 1,000 impressions fall back toward September levels in the Nov 4 – Dec 3 window with no changes on our side, that confirms the election effect.

recommendations.headline: Move YouTube and most of Display into the search campaigns that produce good leads
recommendations.detail: YouTube cost $1,609 with zero clicks and zero conversions (it was $975 with the same result last month). Display cost $2,101, drove 40% of Google's website sessions and produced no good leads in Spark; 5 of its 7 'call leads' have no call duration. Branded, Competitors and Non-Branded search produced all 3 good Google leads. Reallocating roughly $3,700 a month into those search campaigns targets the leads sales can actually work.

recommendations.headline: Give 'Day at Mira Mar' real budget and actually test the Yoga cut
recommendations.detail: Day at Mira Mar delivered 7 leads on 5,192 views (1.35 per 1,000), almost double Sarasota Lifestyle (0.75) and Amenity (0.79). The Yoga and v2 cuts reached only 224 views combined, so the test never ran. Shift weight from Sarasota Lifestyle to Day at Mira Mar and force-deliver Yoga for two weeks before judging it.

recommendations.headline: Judge Meta on good leads, not lead count
recommendations.detail: Meta is the cheapest source of names ($160 platform CPL, $267 per CRM contact) but 1 of 62 contacts is rated good and 31 are Non Responsive. Prospecting – Key Feeder Market (New LP) took the biggest Meta budget ($4,684) for 19 leads. Hold Meta spend flat, tighten feeder-market targeting, and report cost per good lead each month.

recommendations.headline: Follow up the 8 warm buyers that came from paid ads
recommendations.detail: The sales team's buyer list shows 8 Warm prospects that came in through paid ads (6 Google, 1 Meta, 1 LinkedIn), plus 2 that went Cold. Two have already toured the gallery, one more very likely has, and three are planning Sarasota trips between mid-November and late December. Booking those visits is the fastest path to the next contract; the LinkedIn buyer is the newest and should be confirmed first.

recommendations.headline: Report cost per gallery visit and per contract, not just per lead
recommendations.detail: Spark already records signed contracts and sales-gallery visits on each buyer's record. This window logged 17 gallery visits (16 last window); only 2 trace to a paid ad, and the 9 active hard contracts came from branded Google search (2), realtors (2–3), the sales center (2), the website (1) and a Business Observer banner (1) — none from Meta. Ask the sales team to log every visit as "Sales Center Visit" and confirm the source on the most recent realtor-attributed contract so this becomes a monthly cost-per-visit and cost-per-contract view.

recommendations.headline: Phone: find out why Google calls fell 63% and assign callback ownership
recommendations.detail: Calls dropped from 49 to 16; Google Ads calls went from 30 to 11. Check whether call extensions or the call-tracking number changed around the landing-page switch. The answer rate is still 56%, under the 70% floor: 7 of 16 calls were missed.

recommendations.headline: Fix two tracking gaps
recommendations.detail: (1) Two Google contacts carry utm_campaign 'search_competitors?utm_source=google' — a broken final-URL suffix in the Competitors campaign. (2) LinkedIn leads arrive without UTM or zip; hidden fields are being added. Add LinkedIn and Microsoft Ads spend to the dashboard so next month's cost per lead covers every paid channel.

recommendations.headline: Align price messaging in search ads
recommendations.detail: Search headlines say both 'Starting From The $4 Millions' and 'From The High $3 Millions'. Pick one so the ad and the landing page agree.
